recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-13389 unless Patient Care resolves FHIR-23061 or opens a new issue changing Communication's relationship to messaging.
issue_request: FHIR-13389 was a Published Patient Care change request for FHIR-core Communication, raised against STU3 and applied for R5. It asked to clarify whether Communication is an event or workflow resource, when Communication can exist outside CommunicationRequest, when the two resources are duplicative, and when Communication may wrap or accompany exchanged data. The final Persuasive with Modification resolution approved definition, scope/use-case, data-sharing, and CommunicationRequest relationship guidance.
initial_application: Commit f55ce1246f6f94cee3c82bde7721a1e15d8def0a applied the issue in PR #836 by adding the Communication purpose paragraph, use cases, wrapping/accompanying-data note, and CommunicationRequest relationship note, while explicitly omitting the two TBD guidance links. Commit 7c753e02f31f8e55c40f8d5fa5338f31bf357c14 completed that gap by adding the wrapping anchor from Scope and Usage and linking the note to the Approaches to Exchanging FHIR Data decision tree. The current StructureDefinition source carries J#13389 and the approved clinical/business-level definition.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists communication=Communication as an active resource, so the inspected Communication source files are current build inputs. Later applied Communication decisions refined neighboring wording: FHIR-28235/FHIR-40214 replaced the literal FHIR-13389 planned/failed timing phrase with process-initiated wording, and FHIR-40760 restored the Boundaries paragraph to that same later-approved wording family. FHIR-23061 is the broader Communication-vs-MessageHeader boundary tracker referenced by the same discussion trail, but it remains Triaged/Unresolved.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current active source already contains the requested scope paragraph, workflow-event statement, use cases, wrapping/accompanying-data guidance with a real decision-tree link, Communication/CommunicationRequest guidance, and root resource definition. Reverting to the older literal planned/failed sentence or adding duplicate prose would conflict with later applied decisions or create maintenance drift.
